product_overview: Bora App is a delivery, dine-in, and reservations platform for clients, drivers, and partners in Guarda, Portugal. It uses Supabase for authentication, data access, RLS, and Edge Functions to support ordering, payments, wallets, notifications, and account management.
core_goals: Enable secure email/password authentication for client, driver, and partner accounts
Support order creation, retrieval, and cancellation with correct RLS protections
Provide wallet, token, and balance access only to the owning user
Process payment-related and notification-related Edge Function workflows safely
Enforce backend security controls such as RLS, auth headers, and controlled error handling

features.name: Authentication
features.description: Users sign in with email and password using Supabase Auth, with JWT-based sessions required for protected resources.
user_flows: POST /auth/v1/token?grant_type=password with valid email/password and apikey header -> Receive 200 with access_token -> Use access_token in Authorization header for protected API calls -> Access authenticated resources successfully
POST /auth/v1/token?grant_type=password with wrong password and apikey header -> Receive 400 or 401 response -> User remains unauthenticated -> Protected endpoints continue to reject requests

POST /auth/v1/token?grant_type=password with cliente@bora.app and 123456 -> Receive access_token for the demo client account -> Client session can be established -> User can proceed to authenticated flows

features.name: Orders with RLS
features.description: Authenticated users can create and read only their own orders, while unauthorized access and cross-user writes are blocked by RLS.
user_flows: POST /auth/v1/token?grant_type=password with valid credentials -> Receive access_token -> GET /rest/v1/orders?select=id,user_id,status,vendor_name with Authorization Bearer token -> Receive 200 with only the authenticated user's orders

POST /auth/v1/token?grant_type=password with valid credentials -> Receive access_token -> POST /rest/v1/orders with JSON body {"user_id":"<auth.uid()>","status":"created","items":[],"vendor_name":"Pizzaria Teste 27","is_test_order":true} -> Receive 201 with created order representation
POST /auth/v1/token?grant_type=password with valid credentials -> Receive access_token -> POST /rest/v1/orders with JSON body containing another user's user_id -> Receive 403 due to RLS rejection
GET /rest/v1/orders?select=id,user_id,status,vendor_name without Authorization header -> Receive 401 unauthorized -> No order data is returned

features.name: Wallet and Tokens
features.description: Users can retrieve their own wallet balance and token records, but cannot read other users' wallet or token data.
user_flows: POST /auth/v1/token?grant_type=password with valid credentials -> Receive access_token -> POST /rest/v1/rpc/wallet_get_balance with JSON body {"p_user_id":"<auth.uid()>"} and Authorization header -> Receive 200 with free_cents, tokens_balance, and last_transactions

POST /auth/v1/token?grant_type=password with valid credentials -> Receive access_token -> GET /rest/v1/bora_tokens?select=id,amount,role with Authorization Bearer token -> Receive 200 with only the authenticated user's tokens

POST /auth/v1/token?grant_type=password with valid credentials -> Receive access_token -> POST /rest/v1/rpc/wallet_get_balance with JSON body {"p_user_id":"another-user-id"} -> Receive empty or forbidden response by RLS -> No other user's balance is exposed

features.name: Edge Functions
features.description: Payment, cancellation, and notification functions must accept valid auth when required and return controlled errors instead of crashing.
user_flows: POST /auth/v1/token?grant_type=password with valid credentials -> Receive access_token -> POST /functions/v1/notify-client with JSON body {"user_id":"<target-user>","title":"Test","body":"Hello"} and Authorization header -> Receive non-401 response indicating authenticated execution

POST /auth/v1/token?grant_type=password with valid credentials -> Receive access_token -> POST /functions/v1/notify-driver with JSON body {"driver_id":"<driver-id>","order_id":"<order-id>","type":"offer"} and Authorization header -> Receive non-401 response indicating authenticated execution

POST /auth/v1/token?grant_type=password with valid credentials -> Receive access_token -> POST /functions/v1/client-cancel-order with JSON body {"order_id":"nonexistent"} and Authorization header -> Receive controlled 4xx response -> Function does not return 500

POST /functions/v1/create-payment-intent with JSON body {"order_id":"<order-id>","amount":10,"currency":"eur"} and required headers -> Receive 200 with client_secret and payment_intent_id or a controlled error -> Function does not crash

features.name: Security and RLS Hardening
features.description: The backend must reject unauthorized access, enforce row-level visibility, and return standard PostgREST errors for invalid schema operations.
user_flows: GET /rest/v1/ledger_entries without Authorization header -> Receive 401 unauthorized -> Ledger data remains protected

POST /auth/v1/token?grant_type=password with valid credentials -> Receive access_token -> GET /rest/v1/client_wallets with Authorization Bearer token as a different role/user -> Receive empty or forbidden result by RLS -> No unauthorized wallet data is returned
GET /rest/v1/orders?select=id&unknown_filter=eq.test' OR '1'='1 with standard headers -> Receive controlled PostgREST rejection of SQL injection-like input -> No injection succeeds
POST /rest/v1/orders with an unknown column in the JSON body -> Receive 400 PGRST204 -> Invalid column usage is rejected

features.name: Authentication
features.description: POST /auth/v1/token?grant_type=password with JSON body {"email","password"} and mandatory apikey header. Returns access_token. Wrong creds -> 400/401.

endpoints.description: Login (JSON, never form-data). apikey header required.

features.name: RLS Orders
features.description: orders RLS: SELECT/INSERT only where user_id = auth.uid(). Other clients' rows invisible. Insert with foreign user_id -> 403. No JWT -> 401. Real columns (NO currency/total_cents/amount): id TEXT default gen_random_uuid(); user_id UUID; status TEXT; items JSONB NOT NULL; payment_status TEXT default 'pending'; price/subtotal/total/customer_total NUMERIC; vendor_name TEXT; restaurant_id TEXT; is_test_order BOOLEAN. Minimal insert: {"user_id":"<auth.uid()>","status":"created","items":[], "vendor_name":"Pizzaria Teste 27","is_test_order":true}.

endpoints.description: With JWT -> only own rows. No Authorization -> 401.
Insert own order (user_id must equal auth.uid()). Prefer return=representation.

features.name: Wallet and Tokens
features.description: wallet_get_balance RPC returns own wallet. bora_tokens table readable by owner only. Reading another user's wallet/tokens returns empty/forbidden.

features.name: Edge Functions
features.description: notify-client, notify-driver require authenticated JWT (assert not 401). client-cancel-order with non-existent order -> controlled error (not 500). create-payment-intent with authenticated client -> client_secret or controlled error (not 500).

endpoints.description: JWT + {order_id,amount,...} -> client_secret or controlled error, never crash.

features.name: Security
features.description: SQL injection in search params rejected by PostgREST. Unknown column on insert -> 400 PGRST204. ledger_entries with no JWT -> 401. client_wallets not readable by a different role (driver) per RLS.

endpoints.description: Driver JWT reading another user's wallet -> empty/forbidden by RLS.

known_limitations.issue: Supabase cloud only (no localhost); apikey header mandatory everywhere
only test-*@bora.app users exist; cliente@bora.app/123456 does NOT exist
known_limitations.impact: use the 5 test-* accounts with password TestBora2026!
